revisionHistory.issue: Ozaki draft repeated sunlight/rain/title readings and generic collaboration/curation arguments across three articles.
revisionHistory.resolution: All nine localized Ozaki essays rewritten with distinct concrete subject matter; re-read and primary facts independently verified.

revisionHistory.issue: Matsuda/Saito artist essays repeated album-title inventories; song endings repeated provider caveats.
revisionHistory.resolution: Replaced artist inventories with sourced career context and song endings with focused interpretation; all localized replacement passages re-read.

revisionHistory.issue: Kasai J.Cohen full-name expansion could not be reliably independently reconciled between provider variants.
revisionHistory.resolution: Author removed expansion and retained exact Qobuz joint-credit initials.

revisionHistory.issue: Restricted Spotify items risked being treated as usable embeds.
revisionHistory.resolution: Owner final conservative policy moves four candidates out of usable serviceLinks: Ota Spotify album/song, Ota official YouTube song, and Kasai Spotify song. Exact provider evidence and local restriction wording are preserved.

remainingRecommendations.detail: Several articles still use recurring doorway/room/recognition/belonging metaphors and extended title-only interpretation. Shortening these would improve information density, particularly COQUETTISH, Butterfly and Pineapple album essays.
Many accuracy caveats are already in structured metadata. Preserve essential warnings there; avoid repeating all provider/date distinctions in the cultural argument.
演唱者 and 表演 sound less idiomatic than 歌い手, 歌手, 演者, 演技 or 表現 in several passages. Author received exact examples.

sourceLimits.detail: No song lyrics reproduced beyond titles and tiny title-word analysis. SUNSET BEACH and ONE include short conceptual paraphrases, not a line-by-line reconstruction.
Kasai focus-song key change and vocoder interaction are explicitly attributed to Koji Murai. No firsthand listening or transcription is claimed.
Title-order metaphors and broader cultural arguments are authorial interpretation, not attributed artist intent. They should remain labeled as such.
